newsitem.title: SPAIN: Golf-Ballesteros spots new Ryder Cup talent.
newsitem.headline: Golf-Ballesteros spots new Ryder Cup talent.

text.p: European Ryder Cup captain Seve Ballesteros says he has already spotted some promising new talent for next year's match against the United States at Valderrama.
With a host of new young players threatening to take over from the old guard on the European team who will defend the title, Ballesteros has identified at least two potential candidates.
"Thomas Bjorn and Darren Clarke are both looking good," he said on Thursday, referring to the Dane and the Irishman who have both won recent tournaments counting towards positions on the team.
Bjorn, 25, became Denmark's first winner of a European Tour event when he took the Loch Lomond Invitational last month from a field which included Colin Montgomerie, Nick Faldo and Ian Woosnam.

Clarke, 28, won the German Masters earlier this month with a 24-under-par total of 264 and shot 72 to Bjorn's 71 on the first day of the Volvo Masters on Thursday at the same Valderrama course where the Ryder Cup will be played.
Both are big, strong players able to cope with the demands of the layout and are currently second and fourth in the standings. The top 10 will earn automatic spots on the team.
Ballesteros will select two further players.

"There is still a long way to go. The only thing that worries me is all those early season tournaments next year with weak fields where players will be picking up easy points," added the Spaniard, who would like fewer automatic qualifiers and more wild card picks.
Ballesteros, who hopes to play in the Cup himself, will need to improve on his round of 74 following a recent bout of flu.
He yanked his drove at the 10th around to the 18th fairway and had to play a brilliant cut iron shot around a tree to reach the green with his approach before saving par.
But he carved his two-iron tee shot some 50 yards off line and lost it at the 212-yard 12th, then made four with his second ball for a six.
He also had a bogey six at the 17th, where he tried and failed to clear the lake in front of the green with his second shot.
"Six at the 12th really hurt and then I bogeyed the 17th and 18th as a consequence of that," he said.
"Probably I should not have gone for the green with my second shot at 17, but that's the way I am," he added.

Since he returned this spring from a five-month break, Ballesteros has not regained the form which made him one of the world's top players for two decades, despite fourth and third place finishes over the last two months.
"It's not much fun when you can't play as you are supposed to," he said.
"Now I'm looking forward to the finish of the season. Maybe I'll change a couple things in my swing during the winter. I'm looking forward to playing better next year.
